Question:
Could you analyze our data and identify which ten-year period starting from any movie release year present in the data had the largest number of films, considering consecutive ten-year periods beginning at each unique year? Only output the start year and the total count for that specific period.

4 candidates were produced independently. Each shows its SQL and the first rows of its result.

SQL:
WITH distinct_years AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT 
    CASE 
      WHEN year LIKE '% %' THEN TRIM(SUBSTR(year, INSTR(year, ' ') + 1))
      ELSE year
    END as year_num
  FROM Movie
),
movie_years AS (
  SELECT MID, 
    CASE 
      WHEN year LIKE '% %' THEN TRIM(SUBSTR(year, INSTR(year, ' ') + 1))
      ELSE year
    END as year_num
  FROM Movie
),
period_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    dy.year_num as start_year,
    COUNT(my.MID) as film_count
  FROM distinct_years dy
  JOIN movie_years my ON CAST(dy.year_num AS INTEGER) <= CAST(my.year_num AS INTEGER)
    AND CAST(my.year_num AS INTEGER) <= CAST(dy.year_num AS INTEGER) + 9
  GROUP BY dy.year_num
)
SELECT start_year, film_count FROM period_counts ORDER BY film_count DESC LIMIT 1

WITH valid_years AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT year 
    FROM Movie 
    WHERE year GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]'
),
valid_movies AS (
    SELECT year 
    FROM Movie 
    WHERE year GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]'
),
period_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        vy.year as start_year,
        COUNT(m.year) as film_count
    FROM valid_years vy
    LEFT JOIN valid_movies m ON CAST(m.year AS INTEGER) >= CAST(vy.year AS INTEGER) 
        AND CAST(m.year AS INTEGER) <= CAST(vy.year AS INTEGER) + 9
    GROUP BY vy.year
)
SELECT start_year, film_count
FROM (
    SELECT start_year, film_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY film_count DESC) as rn
    FROM period_counts
) ranked
WHERE rn = 1

    GROUP BY y.start_year
)

FROM period_counts
